newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus combats water shortage with desalination.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus combats water shortage with desalination.

text.p: Cyprus plans to build three more desalination plants before the turn of the century to combat an acute water shortage affecting the holiday island, officials said on Wednesday.
The plans will increase the number of units to four, including one which is nearing completion and due to come on stream by April.
"It won't solve the water shortage but will certainly ease it," Agriculture Minister Costas Petrides told reporters.
Water reserves in the island's reservoirs are rapidly depleting while rainfall, the island's only source for water, has been minimal this winter.
Tenders for the construction of the first of the three new plants will be invited in April after specifications are prepared, Petrides said.

It is to be constructed east of the southern coastal town of Larnaca under a build-operate-transfer (BOT) contract which will sell desalinated water to the government for a period of time, becoming state property thereafter, Petrides said.

The other two units will be based in Limassol, also on the southern coast, and the western coastal resort of Paphos. Both towns are popular tourist destinations where demand for water, especially in summer, is high.
The first plant which will be ready in April is being built by Cyprus's Caramondanis Company.

Petrides said provisions have been made to increase the daily output of the existing unit, west of Larnaca, to 40,000 tonnes by June 1998 from an expected 25,000 tonnes it will produce when it starts operating. The existing plant will operate under a BOT contract for 10 years.
